## What's new in 2.3.3

This release cuts idle memory use, stops Snipping Tool screenshots from being optimized more than once, and hardens logging.

### Fixes

**Much lower memory use (idle and while optimizing)**
Squish could sit at around 2.5 GB of RAM while idle. The cause was large-image quality scoring, which allocated big buffers on every pass and kept them committed after the work was done.
- The perceptual quality scorer (SSIMULACRA2) now reuses its buffers and blurs in place. It scores color channels one after another instead of allocating separate buffers for each in parallel. Opaque images are scored directly, without extra copies.
- The JPEG searches share one verifier, and only one decode-and-score runs at a time.
- PNG palette probes still run side by side, but they decode and score one candidate at a time.
- Squish now runs a compacting garbage collection after 3 seconds with no work running or queued, so freed memory goes back to Windows.
- The ImageMagick memory limit is now 512 MB, down from 40% of RAM.
- Video quality search scores each ffmpeg frame as it arrives instead of holding every full-resolution frame.
- In test measurements, one 1080p quality score now allocates about 63 MB, down from roughly 2 GB per screenshot in the original report.

**Snipping Tool screenshots no longer get optimized repeatedly**
A single snip could trigger several optimization runs, because Windows writes the image to the clipboard more than once. Squish now:
- waits 200 ms (max 750 ms) for image clipboard changes to settle, instead of 25 ms. Text and file copies are unchanged.
- recognizes repeats of the same image by content and drops them before writing any file. It compares both the PNG bytes and the decoded pixels, so re-encoded copies of the same snip still match.
- cancels older in-flight jobs when a different image replaces them (with Auto-copy on).
- deletes the result and temp file of a cancelled job that finishes anyway, so nothing is left behind in `%APPDATA%\Squish\images`.

### Security
- Log messages from the cross-app automation host are now sanitized to prevent log forging (CR/LF injection through untrusted values).

### Encoder tools
- Updated **libavif** to 1.4.2.
- Kept **gifsicle** at 1.95. Version 1.97 broke `--lossy` (it barely shrinks anything), and upstream fixed it in 1.98. Automatic tool updates now skip 1.97 and will pick up 1.98 when a Windows build is available.

### Tests
- Added large-image tests for the SSIMULACRA2 scorer, including a regression score pinned from the original implementation.
- Added 13 clipboard dedup unit tests and a clipboard-gated monitor test.
- Added log sanitizer tests for the automation host.

### Known issues
- jpegli 0.12.0 no longer ships `cjpegli.exe` in its archive, so Squish stays on the current jpegli until that is resolved.
